slots.label: Tenths
entries: Tenths: one bar, ten equal parts: split one whole bar into ten equal parts and shade four - that shaded amount is 0.4, four tenths.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Hundredths
entries: Hundredths: one square, one hundred tiny parts: split the whole square into ten rows and ten columns and shade twenty-five tiny parts - 0.20 plus 0.05 is 0.25.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Add: line up the places
entries: Add: line up the places: write 0.4 as 0.40, line up tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths, then add to get 0.40 + 0.25 = 0.65.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Watch out: 0.25 is not bigger than 0.4
entries: Watch out: 0.25 is not bigger than 0.4: compare the covered amounts, not the digit counts - forty hundredths covers more of the whole than twenty-five hundredths.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Tenths
entries: The first place after the decimal point: the whole split into ten equal parts, so each part is one tenth and 0.4 is four tenths.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Hundredths
entries: The second place after the decimal point: the whole split into one hundred tiny parts, so 0.25 is twenty-five hundredths.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Place value
entries: What a digit is worth because of where it stands: the same 4 is worth four tenths in 0.4 and would be worth four hundredths in 0.04.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Decimal point
entries: The dot that separates the wholes from the tenths: everything to its right is less than one whole.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
